passages.context: Jerome's quotation of the Gospel according to the Hebrews, read in the retrieved transcription with the surrounding account of James's death and burial in view. Registered as a second-century tradition that knew the burial wrappings had been left behind and accounted for them narratively rather than evidentially.
passages.notes: The sentence continues in the source with the parenthesis about James's oath and then the bread narrative; the transcription stops at the clause bearing on the grave clothes.

work.author: Jerome
work.description: Jerome's catalogue of Christian writers, completed about 393. Chapter 2, on James the brother of the Lord, quotes the lost Gospel according to the Hebrews, which said that the risen Lord gave his grave clothes to the servant of the priest before appearing to James. A locus is the chapter number.
work.title: De viris illustribus
